title: STAMP as a topology-aware molecular language for fragment-level learning and editing
abstract: arXiv:2610.18438v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Molecular fragments provide chemically meaningful units, but existing molecular languages rarely make their locations and connections explicit for editing. Here we introduce STAMP (Sequential Tree Attachment-based Motif-Preserving representation), a topology-aware molecular language that connects fragment-level representation learning with precise structural editing. STAMP separately encodes motif identity, attachment sites and tree topology, making fragments reusable across contexts and subtrees directly accessible. Learned representations capture motif similarity and recurring transformations, and lower activity-cliff prediction error on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder. Compatible subtree operations support scaffold-preserving optimization, ranking first among six methods on 15 of 23 benchmark objectives. A deterministic compiler enables frozen language models to act on indexed fragments, improving molecular editing,

translated_title: STAMP：一种用于片段级学习与编辑的拓扑感知分子语言
translated_abstract: 分子片段提供了具有化学意义的单元，但现有的分子语言很少将片段的位置和连接关系显式表达出来以供编辑。本文提出了STAMP（基于序列化树连接的基序保持表示，Sequential Tree Attachment-based Motif-Preserving representation），这是一种拓扑感知的分子语言，将片段级表示学习与精确的结构编辑联系起来。STAMP分别编码基序身份、连接位点和树拓扑结构，使片段可在不同上下文中复用，并可直接访问子树。所学到的表示能够捕捉基序相似性和重复出现的转换模式，与同等配置的SMILES编码器相比，在30个靶点中的23个上降低了活性悬崖（activity cliff）预测误差。兼容的子树操作支持保持骨架（scaffold-preserving）的分子优化，在23个基准目标中的15个上于六种方法中排名第一。一个确定性的编译器使冻结的语言模型能够对已索引的片段进行操作，从而改进分子编辑。
tldr: STAMP是一种拓扑感知的分子语言，通过分别编码基序、连接位点与树拓扑结构，将片段级表示学习与精确的分子结构编辑统一起来，在活性悬崖预测和保持骨架的分子优化等任务上显著优于现有方法。
en_tdlr: STAMP is a topology-aware molecular language that separately encodes motif identity, attachment sites, and tree topology, unifying fragment-level representation learning with precise structural editing and outperforming existing methods on activity-cliff prediction and scaffold-preserving molecular optimization.
